title: ClickFix fake-CAPTCHA lure leading to StealC infostealer

source.telemetry: Windows Sysmon (Event ID 13, registry SetValue) via Wazuh agent
source.detection: Wazuh rule 100700 -- ClickFix: RunMRU entry containing remote-execution command
source.provenance_note: Constructed from published ClickFix campaign reporting. The telemetry field shapes mirror what the windows_eventchannel decoder emits on this lab's real agent (doubled backslashes normalised for display). No live malware was executed to produce this.

intel.summary: A fake CAPTCHA or browser error page uses JavaScript to silently write a long PowerShell or mshta command to the victim's clipboard, then instructs them to press Win+R, Ctrl+V, Enter. The victim executes the attacker's command themselves, which sidesteps most download and macro controls entirely.
observed_kill_chain: Victim lands on compromised site or malvertised page showing a fake CAPTCHA
Page JavaScript writes the payload command to the clipboard
Victim pastes into the Run dialog (Win+R) and presses Enter
RunMRU registry key records what was typed -- key forensic artifact
intel.evasion_note: The command builds 'irm' (Invoke-RestMethod) via runtime string substitution and pipes the response to 'iex', so the retrieved payload executes in memory and never lands on disk under a recognisable download syntax.

technique: User Execution: Malicious Copy and Paste

alert.description: ClickFix: RunMRU entry contains remote-execution command (paste-to-run lure)

analyst_note: The trailing 'Verification ID' text is padding the lure page appends so the Run dialog visually truncates the real command. RunMRU is the strongest artifact here because it survives the process exiting.
